CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFSERVLETPARAM

NEW IN KOLDFUSION 4.5

CFSERVLETPARAM tags go inside a CFSERVLET block. With VALUE, the tag adds a request parameter, which the servlet reads with getParameter. With VARIABLE, it passes a CFML variable by reference as a request attribute (read with getAttribute); when the servlet stores a new value with setAttribute, the variable is updated after the CFSERVLET tag.

Category

Extensibility

Syntax

<CFSERVLETPARAM NAME="parameter_name"
    VALUE="value">

<CFSERVLETPARAM NAME="servlet_attribute_name"
    VARIABLE="variable_name"
    TYPE="INT/DOUBLE/BOOL/DATE/STRING">

Attributes

NAME
Required. Name of the parameter, or of the servlet attribute when passing by reference.
VALUE
Optional. Value passed as a request parameter. Use either VALUE or VARIABLE.
VARIABLE
Optional. Name (not value) of a CFML variable passed by reference as a servlet attribute.
TYPE
Optional. Java type of a VARIABLE: INT (java.lang.Integer), DOUBLE (java.lang.Double), BOOL (java.lang.Boolean), DATE (java.util.Date) or STRING (java.lang.String). Without TYPE, simple values are passed as strings, arrays as java.util.Vector and structures as java.util.Hashtable.

Usage

Queries cannot be passed to servlets (ColdFusion used a WDDX RecordSet class that KoldFusion does not have); pass the columns as arrays instead. Outside a CFSERVLET tag, CFSERVLETPARAM raises a context validation error.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Visitor = "Netscape 4.7 user">
<CFSET Wishlist = ListToArray("Zip drive,56K modem,Palm V")>
<CFTRY>
  <!--- SnoopServlet (in java/samples) lists everything it receives --->
  <CFSERVLET CODE="SnoopServlet" WRITEOUTPUT="No">
    <CFSERVLETPARAM NAME="page" VALUE="cfservletparam.cfm">
    <CFSERVLETPARAM NAME="visitor" VARIABLE="Visitor" TYPE="STRING">
    <CFSERVLETPARAM NAME="wishlist" VARIABLE="Wishlist">
  </CFSERVLET>
  <CFOUTPUT>
  <P>SnoopServlet sent back #Len(CFSERVLET.Output)# bytes:</P>
  #CFSERVLET.Output#
  </CFOUTPUT>
  <CFCATCH TYPE="Any">
    <CFOUTPUT>
    <P>The servlet could not run, so the parameters went nowhere.<BR>
    <I>#CFCATCH.Message#</I></P>
    <P>The variable passed by reference still says: <B>#Visitor#</B></P>
    </CFOUTPUT>
  </CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
